title: Regular principal generic fibre gives a continuous Jacobian splitting up to a power
statement: Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, let $r\geq0$, and put $P=\widehat{k[t,x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_{(t)}$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $J\subseteq P$ be an ideal and write $B=P/J$. Suppose $B[1/t]$ is a regular Noetherian ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]; localization here inverts the powers of the image of $t$. Define the $B$-linear map $\delta:J/J^2\to B^{\oplus r}$ by $f\bmod J^2\mapsto(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod J)_i$, with derivatives defined continuously by differentiating polynomial approximations. Then there exist $c\geq0$ and a $B$-linear map $h:B^{\oplus r}\to J/J^2$ such that $h\delta=t^c\operatorname{id}_{J/J^2}$. No assertion that $\operatorname{coker}\delta$ is torsion is made.

proof.text: The polynomial ring $k[t,x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], using only its Noetherianity clause. Its $(t)$-adic completion $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose generators $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ of $J$, allowing $s=0$.

source.place: Tags 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring), 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian); finite generation is the definition of Noetherianity

proof.text:
Put $K=k((t))$ with $|t|=1/2$. From the inverse-limit definition [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], an element of $P$ is a series $\sum_

u\in k[[t]]$ such that, modulo any $t^n$, only finitely many coefficients are nonzero. Equivalently $a_

Since the valuation is discrete, one common power of $t$ moves all coefficients into $k[[t]]$. Thus coefficient expansion gives $P[1/t]=K\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle=:A$. The Laurent-series field is complete: in a Cauchy sequence every coefficient below any fixed exponent eventually stabilizes, and a common lower bound follows by comparing its tail with one fixed term. The stabilized coefficients therefore define its limit. Fractions give $B[1/t]\cong A/JA=:C$: surjectivity follows by choosing representatives, and a fraction maps to zero precisely when some power of $t$ times its numerator lies in $J$. Termwise $x_i$-derivatives preserve the restricted condition, since integers have norm at most $1$; reduction modulo each $t^n$ verifies Leibniz from polynomials. Hence these derivatives agree with the continuously defined derivatives in the statement.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 proof, printed p.19; explicit coefficient and fraction verification by Q06

proof.text: By hypothesis $C=B[1/t]$ is regular Noetherian. Apply [lem-per-regular-affinoid-complete-field-extension] to the Tate presentation $C=A/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$. The field $K=k((t))$ has characteristic zero, is complete and has nontrivial discrete absolute value by Step 2. Therefore for every complete isometric extension $L/K$, the coefficient-extended quotient $L\langle x\rangle/(f_{1,L},\ldots,f_{s,L})$ is regular Noetherian.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 proof, printed p.19, regular affinoid implies smooth over the perfect field

proof.text:
For $E\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}$ and $T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of equal cardinality, put $J_E=(f_j:j\in E)\subseteq P$, $D_{E,T}=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i\in T,j\in E}\in P$, and
$$H=\sum_{E,T}\overline{(J_E:J)}\,\overline{D_{E,T}}\,B,$$
where $(J_E:J)=\{a\in P:aJ\subseteq J_E\}$ and bars mean reduction modulo $J$. The coefficient extension property from Step 3 is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-per-geometric-affinoid-jacobian-unit]. Applied over $K$ to $C=A/JA$, it says that the analogous ideal $H_K$, using colons and minors in $A$, equals $C$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2, printed pp.20--21, Jacobian ideal formula and analytic criterion

proof.text:
We check $H_K=HC$ without assuming $t$ is a non-zero-divisor on $B$. Inclusion $HC\subseteq H_K$ follows by localizing $aJ\subseteq J_E$. Conversely let $a/t^d\in(J_EA:JA)$ with $a\in P$. For each of the finitely many generators $f_j$ of $J$, membership $af_j/1\in J_EA$ means that $t^{N_j}af_j\in J_E$ for some $N_j\geq0$, by the equality rule for fractions [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Taking $N=\max_j N_j$ (take $N=0$ if $s=0$) gives $t^Na\in(J_E:J)$. Thus every localized colon element comes from its colon in $P$. The derivative minors are the same after localization, proving the equality of ideals. Since $HC=C$, a finite sum representing $1$ in this ideal has a common denominator and gives $u/t^d=1$ with $u\in H$. Equality of fractions gives $t^e(u-t^d)=0$ in $B$ for some $e\geq0$. Therefore $t^{e+d}=t^eu\in H$. Set $c=e+d$ and write
$$t^c=\sum_{\lambda=1}^q b_\lambda\bar a_\lambda\bar D_{E_\lambda,T_\lambda},\quad b_\lambda\in B,\quad a_\lambda J\subseteq J_{E_\lambda}.$$
The finite sum exists by the definition of the generated ideal.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed p.20, compatibility with localization; explicit finite-generator and denominator argument by Q06

proof.text:
Write $M=J/J^2$. Fix one summand $a=a_\lambda$, $E=E_\lambda$, $T=T_\lambda$, and form the square matrix $U=(\overline{\partial f_j/\partial x_i})_{i\in T,j\in E}$ over $B$. Let $q_E:B^{E}\to M$ send the $j$th basis vector to $[f_j]$, and let $p_T:B^r\to B^T$ be coordinate projection, identifying the ordered sets $E,T$ with the same finite index set. Define the $B$-linear map
$$h_{a,E,T}=q_E\operatorname{adj}(U)\bar a\,p_T:B^r\to M.$$
For any $f\in J$, choose $v_j\in P$ with $af=\sum_{j\in E}v_jf_j$, which is possible because $aJ\subseteq J_E$. Modulo $J^2$ this reads $\bar a[f]=\sum_j\bar v_j[f_j]$. Differentiating and reducing modulo $J$ gives $\bar a\,p_T\delta([f])=U(\bar v_j)_j$: the terms involving $f$ or any $f_j$ vanish. By [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity], $\operatorname{adj}(U)U=\det(U)\,1$, so
$$h_{a,E,T}\delta([f])=\bar D_{E,T}\sum_j\bar v_j[f_j]=\bar a\bar D_{E,T}[f].$$
The formula for $h_{a,E,T}$ is independent of choices of the $v_j$. For $E=T=\varnothing$ take the zero map; the colon condition gives $aJ=0$, so the same equality holds with empty determinant $1$.

source.place: Tag 0GAJ (lemma-equivalent-with-artin-smooth), condition (4) to (3); direct adjugate calculation by Q06; matrix identity is algebra.tex Tag 07DQ (lemma-matrix-left-inverse)

proof.text:
Set $h=\sum_{\lambda=1}^q b_\lambda h_{a_\lambda,E_\lambda,T_\lambda}$. This finite sum is $B$-linear, and Steps 5--6 give
$$h\delta=\sum_\lambda b_\lambda\bar a_\lambda\bar D_{E_\lambda,T_\lambda}\operatorname{id}_M=t^c\operatorname{id}_M.$$
This is the required conclusion. If $C=0$, Step 5 gives a power of $t$ equal to zero in $B$, and $h=0$ also suffices. No step uses torsion of the cokernel of $\delta$.
